title: Mirror Biology and Cyberbiosecurity: New Frontiers, Risks, and Strategic Responses
content: Mirror biology is the creation of synthetic organisms composed entirely of mirror-image biomolecules, such as D-amino acids and L-sugars, in contrast to the natural use of L-amino acids and D-sugars. Though this novel field promises significant advances in medicine, biomanufacturing, and environmental applications due to the enhanced stability and immune evasion of mirror organisms, its features raise unprecedented biosecurity risks, particularly when combined with cybersecurity vulnerabilities in the digital infrastructures used to design, synthesise, and control mirror life. We mapped the mirror biology development pipeline, from genetic circuit design and cloud-based bioinformatics to automated laboratory systems, to examine the unprecedented biosecurity risks associated with mirror biology. We highlighted key cyber biosecurity vulnerabilities, including data manipulation, unauthorised access, and firmware tampering. Case studies illustrate specific risks such as tampering with genetic design tools and introducing harmful DNA sequences into supply chains. The paper reviews existing technological safeguards, including encryption, zero-trust architectures, AI-enabled anomaly detection, and governance mechanisms such as biosafety oversight and redline enforcement. It emphasises the need for inclusive governance, capacity building, and international collaboration to ensure that mirror biology is not pursued as a field of organism- level research.
